items.title: Blocked-episode migration has no deterministic cutover state machine
items.statement: The migration is conditioned on blocked-episode identity being available, but availability, cutover ownership, mixed old/new record handling, in-flight request disposition, and the point at which legacy identifiers become invalid are not defined.
items.impact: Concurrent or partially upgraded callers can approve different logical episodes, reject valid approvals, or keep request-centric identity alive indefinitely.
items.builder_discretion: Define an atomic, versioned cutover protocol with preconditions, dual-read limits, terminal legacy behavior, and an idempotent migration marker.

evidence.exact_quote:

  identity is available; graph HITL command payload identity moves to
  blocked-episode anchored identity while preserving Contracts_V0 compatibility
  notes for the request-centric migration.

items.title: Approval identity migration omits authorization and anti-replay rules
items.statement: The canonical identity anchor is named, but the unit does not specify which principal may issue, resume, cancel, or supersede a blocked-episode command, nor how stale blocked_sequence or attempt_id payloads are rejected.
items.impact: A correctly shaped but stale, cross-run, or unauthorized command can be accepted against the wrong blocked episode.
items.builder_discretion: Bind every command to an authenticated principal, execution-unit context, monotonic blocked sequence, current episode status, and replay-safe command identifier.

evidence.exact_quote:
- Approval identity stops depending on tier_id, request-centric HITL, or request_id after blocked-episode identity is available.
  - Graph HITL command payloads use blocked-episode anchored identity.
  - Contracts_V0 compatibility notes for request-centric to blocked-episode migration are preserved.

items.title: Identity migration has no partial-failure recovery or rollback contract
items.statement: No behavior is defined for a crash between persistence and graph update, retry after ambiguous acknowledgement, incompatible consumer, or rollback after some payload producers have switched.
items.impact: Approval truth can diverge across persistence, graph state, and GUI consumers with no deterministic reconciliation path.
items.builder_discretion: Specify transaction boundaries, idempotency keys, reconciliation precedence, retry outcomes, and whether rollback is forbidden after the first canonical episode write.

items.title: The 2-of-3 rule does not define eligible or independent corroborators
items.statement: The text counts three votes without defining who or what may vote, independence requirements, duplicate-provider or duplicate-evidence handling, evidence freshness, abstention, confidence, or conflict-of-interest exclusion.
items.impact: Two correlated or attacker-controlled observations can manufacture canonical high-impact truth.
items.builder_discretion: Define voter eligibility, independence domains, evidence lineage, freshness, deduplication, and authority to open or close corroboration.

evidence.exact_quote:
Corroboration disagreement handling uses the 2-of-3 rule: 2-of-3 accepts a

  accepted as blocking or canonical truth, and credible lesser concerns still
  emit a non-blocking minor advisory visible on the Orchestrator page.

items.title: Corroboration has no timeout, reversal, or late-evidence transition semantics
items.statement: The accepted/not-accepted outcomes omit pending, timed-out, withdrawn, superseded, reopened, and revoked states, including what happens when a second or third result arrives after action was taken.
items.impact: The same evidence set can produce unstable blocking and canonical outcomes across retries or arrival order.
items.builder_discretion: Define a monotonic transition table, deadline policy, deterministic ordering, revocation effects, and recovery when previously canonical evidence is invalidated.

items.title: Minor-advisory GUI truth and lifecycle are underspecified
items.statement: Visibility is required, but the Orchestrator presentation does not define pending/loading/stale/offline states, source and timestamp disclosure, dismissal persistence, later escalation or revocation, accessible announcement, or localized severity copy.
items.impact: Operators may interpret a stale or incomplete advisory as current non-blocking truth, and assistive-technology or localized users may miss the state entirely.
items.builder_discretion: Expose provenance, freshness, lifecycle state, and action consequences with non-color-only status, programmatic labels, and localization-safe copy.

items.title: Help cluster and alias resolution contract is incomplete
items.statement: The vocabulary list does not define canonical identifiers, normalization, exact matching, collision precedence, versioning, unknown-token behavior, deep-link stability, alias deprecation, or whether user-provided route text is treated as untrusted input.
items.impact: Malformed, localized, or legacy tokens can resolve to the wrong help topic, create broken links, or become an injection surface in route or rendered-help consumers.
items.builder_discretion: Use immutable topic IDs, an allowlisted alias table, explicit normalization, safe rendering, collision rejection, and versioned deprecation behavior.

items.statement: Related links and aliases have no keyboard/focus, screen-reader naming, bidirectional-text, translation-key, fallback-locale, missing-content, or offline-cache behavior.
items.impact: Users can lose access to required definitions by input modality, locale, or network state, while aliases drift between translated labels and canonical routes.
items.builder_discretion: Specify semantic link roles, focus order, stable translation keys, locale-independent route IDs, offline fallback, and deterministic missing-topic treatment.

items.title: Retained cleanup is a predicate list, not a complete lifecycle
items.statement: The unit defines reasons to enter retained but omits the source states, reason precedence, multiple simultaneous reasons, exit criteria, terminal states, expiry, re-evaluation triggers, and whether retained can be re-entered after cleanup begins.
items.impact: Lanes may be retained forever, cleaned while a reason remains active, or oscillate under changing review and promotion inputs.
items.builder_discretion: Define the full state machine with reason-set semantics, guarded transitions, expiry policy, and deterministic re-evaluation events.

items.title: Cleanup retention lacks race, lease, and destructive-action protection
items.statement: No concurrency contract prevents a cleanup worker from deleting outputs while review, corroboration, or manual retention is being activated; no lease, compare-and-swap, tombstone, undo window, or partial-delete recovery is stated.
items.impact: Irreplaceable lane outputs can be destroyed after a valid retention reason exists or left partially deleted with misleading retained state.
items.builder_discretion: Require an atomic retention check under a cleanup lease, monotonic generation guard, durable deletion journal, quarantine or undo interval, and idempotent recovery.

items.title: Manual retention has no authorization, audit, or privacy boundary
items.statement: The plan does not identify who may activate, extend, or release manual retention, whether approval is required, how the reason is audited, or how retention is bounded by privacy deletion and data-minimization obligations.
items.impact: An unauthorized or forgotten hold can retain sensitive lane outputs indefinitely, while an unauthorized release can enable destructive cleanup.
items.builder_discretion: Define role and scope checks, immutable audit events, reason and expiry fields, renewal policy, legal/privacy precedence, and emergency release controls.

evidence.exact_quote: - "Lane cleanup must not be immediate when retained conditions are active."

items.title: Scale and resource limits are absent for retained lanes and help clusters
items.statement: No upper bounds, eviction policy, quota behavior, backpressure, pagination, indexing limit, or overload response is defined for accumulated retained outputs, corroboration records, advisories, or related-link graphs.
items.impact: Manual holds or unresolved concerns can grow storage and UI query costs without bound, and dense help graphs can degrade navigation or render cycles.
items.builder_discretion: Define quotas and measured limits, safe backpressure, paginated retrieval, bounded graph traversal, and operator-visible saturation behavior.

dimension_assessments.summary: Document surfaces are named, but the producer/consumer set and version-skew obligations are not enumerated.
Cutover, corroboration, and retention omit necessary intermediate, terminal, reversal, and expiry transitions.
No atomicity or lease prevents identity split-brain, arrival-order disagreement, or cleanup racing retention.
Cross-surface migration and destructive cleanup lack crash and ambiguous-acknowledgement outcomes.
No reconciliation, replay, undo, or rollback boundary is defined for migrated identity, revised corroboration, or partial cleanup.
Command principals, corroborator eligibility, and manual-retention authority are undefined; bridge non-ownership is explicitly bounded.
Manual retention and DecisionRecord data have no classification, expiry, redaction, deletion, or privacy-precedence rules.
Approval payload replay and help-token normalization/rendering are not constrained against hostile or malformed input.
Advisory and Decisions views omit provenance, freshness, permission, loading, stale, offline, and absence semantics.
No offline behavior is specified for corroboration arrival, help content, advisory freshness, or DecisionRecord visibility.
Retention, corroboration, advisory, and help-graph storage and query growth are unbounded.
Required user-visible advisories and help links lack semantic, keyboard, focus, and announcement contracts.
Canonical help aliases and GUI state copy lack locale-independent keys, fallback, and bidirectional-text behavior.
Legacy identity cutover and DecisionRecord serialization lack versioned compatibility and mixed-version behavior; bridge scope is appropriately retired.
No diagnostic telemetry, alerts, correlation, or recovery runbooks make the new rules operationally supportable.
Cleanup lacks atomic retention guards, quarantine, undo, and partial-deletion recovery.
Owner and implementation surfaces are listed without executable cross-document convergence or consumer fixtures.
Plan-index and migration checks cannot falsify the runtime, GUI, accessibility, race, or recovery claims; lineage-only notes correctly disclaim proof.
Truncated authoritative prose prevents reliable interpretation and may conceal additional constraints.
